newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls, UAW to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls, UAW to resume talks.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc said it will resume talks Wednesday with the United Auto Workers union aimed at settling day-old strikes at two seat manufacturing plants.

Talks are scheduled to resume at 1400 EST between the company and representatives of workers at the Plymouth, Michigan plant, which makes seats for the Ford Motor Co Expedition, a popular sport/utility vehicle.
Talks are also expected to resume to settle a strike by workers at the Oberlin, Ohio-plant, which makes seats for the Ford Econoline van, the company said.
Ford said Tuesday it would not accept seats made by non-union replacement workers at the plants.
The Plymouth plant employs about 300 hourly workers and the Oberlin plant about 200.
Workers at both plants are seeking inititial contracts, after receiving UAW representation last summer. The workers went on strike early Tuesday morning, after talks stalled.
Johnson Controls would not say what terms it had offered the union.
A UAW spokesman said Tuesday the union is seeking wage parity with other seat suppliers, like Lear Corp, which he said pays $14-$16 an hour.
Johnson Controls shares were down 1 at 85-5/8 Wednesday.
